steps.head: topic
steps.cap: The topic comes first. News goes only with a primary source, a tip is taken from a narrow hook. The post's form rotates so the posts don't look alike.

steps.head: author writes
steps.cap: The author offers three angles, takes the sharpest and writes a draft for it.

steps.head: code check
steps.cap: Code reads the draft without a model: clichés, "in my opinion", a template question at the end, dashes, length and opening. It fixes dashes itself and passes the rest to the editor.
steps.foot: 3 remarks found, code fixed one itself

steps.head: editor by checklist
steps.cap: The editor scores on a scale from 1 to 10 and rewrites. If it can't be pulled above 6, the post is dropped. Then code checks again.

steps.head: ready to show

steps.head: decision
steps.cap: I approve with one button.

steps.head: channel
steps.cap: The post is queued. The bot checks the clock every minute and sends it to the channel in its slot.

steps.head: learning
steps.cap: Every edit of mine and every reason for rejection is saved as a "was → now" pair and teaches the next drafts.

cols.s: Yandex Disk, checked once a day at night
1024 characters, overlap 100, each with its own context line

steps.cap: At night, on a schedule, the bot looks at the folder on the Disk. Only doc, docx, txt and pdf are taken, the rest is skipped.
Clean text is extracted from each file.
The text is cut into chunks of 1024 characters with an overlap of 100. A context line is added to each chunk: which section it belongs to.
A vector is computed for each chunk.
Chunks with metadata (path, md5) go into the vector database. The counter grows.
The next night there's a new file in the folder. Old ones are checked by md5: unchanged, so they're skipped. The new one goes down the lane.
The price list was updated. The md5 is different: the file's old chunks are deleted, and it goes down the lane again.
